Rejected as triggers (do not retry these): bogus store_id -> NULL_REFERENCE (NullReferenceException); currency=XXX -> INVALID_OPERATION (InvalidOperationException); bogus cart_id / product id / order_number / checkout_id -> UCP-level rejections that never reach xAPI; limit out of range, inverted price_min/price_max and unknown language -> accepted silently; create_cart with a non-existent product_id -> ignored, cart created successfully. [KQL] KQL the XAPI span dimensions + the exceptions table for that trace.

The XAPI span has vc.xapi.error.count>0 and reports failure, with vc.xapi.error.codes/.paths populated {SPEC}.
NO exception event on the span, NO exceptions row, NO EventId 2001 log — no synthetic stack trace is fabricated {SPEC}.
SUPPORTING evidence 2026-08-17 on VirtoCommerce.UCP 3.1005.0-pr-6-6c60: the reverse direction holds — expected rejections (product_not_found, cart_not_found, order_not_found, missing_store_id) produce vc.ucp.outcome=rejected with NO exceptions row, no exception.* attributes and stack length 0; for get_product the UCP span is success=False/product_not_found while its child XAPI span is success=True, i.e. xAPI ran fine and nothing was fabricated (2026-08-17) {OBSERVED}. This is the negative twin of UCPO-005: same observable set, opposite expectation.
Once a trigger is confirmed, the pair discriminates AC-3 from AC-4.

References: VCST-5544 AC-4 — trigger still not identified on vcst-qa as of 2026-08-17; needs a controlled fixture from the implementing developer. Reverse evidence gathered (see Assertions). Audited: 2026-08-17.

Title: A failed REST operation returns a usable correlation handle to the caller
Preconditions: vcst-qa with VirtoCommerce.UCP >= 3.1005.0 (PR vc-module-ucp#6) AND VirtoCommerce.OpenTelemetry >= 3.1001.0-alpha.6-vcst-5641 (PR vc-module-opentelemetry#2) both LIVE per /api/platform/modules; VirtoCommerce.ApplicationInsights installed; UCP:Observability:InputCaptureMode=ErrorsOnly; UCP:Observability:EnableApplicationInsightsCompatibilityBridge=true.

Steps:
[HTTP] POST /ucp/v1/catalog/search {store_id:"NO-SUCH-STORE-XYZ",query:"bolt"} (the xAPI-error passthrough path).
[HTTP] POST the same with no store_id (a UCP rejection).
[VERIFY] For each response, look for a correlation identifier and try to use it as operation_Id in App Insights.
Assertions:
EXPECTED: a caller who hits a failure can obtain an identifier that resolves the trace in App Insights, matching the MCP transport which returns "Trace ID: <32-hex>" {SPEC}.
CORRECTION 2026-08-17 — the 2026-08-12 reading of this case was WRONG and is retracted. Source: UcpServiceBase.GetCorrelationId() returns FirstNotEmpty(GetHeader("X-Correlation-Id"), HttpContext?.TraceIdentifier). Verified live on VirtoCommerce.UCP 3.1005.0-pr-6-6c60: a request that sends X-Correlation-Id gets that exact value echoed back in correlation_id on BOTH the REST failure path (400 missing_store_id) and the REST success path (200); with no such header the response falls back to the ASP.NET HttpContext.TraceIdentifier (e.g. 0HNNSHKSHRA31:00000002), which does not resolve in Application Insights. So the REST path DOES offer a usable handle to any caller that supplies one; the residual defect is only the fallback value. The MCP transport does not use correlation_id for this at all — it returns _meta.trace_id, a real 32-hex W3C trace id, which is what the REST fallback should arguably mirror (Activity.Current.TraceId) (2026-08-17) {OBSERVED}.
Cross_Layer_Checks: Compare directly with UCPO-004, where the MCP transport does return a usable 32-hex TraceId.
Failure_Signals: No identifier in a failure response; an identifier that does not resolve in App Insights.
References: VCST-5544 — scope narrowed 2026-08-17: NOT failing as originally recorded on 2026-08-12 (that reading was based only on requests that never sent X-Correlation-Id). Remaining ask is that the no-header fallback be a W3C trace id rather than HttpContext.TraceIdentifier. Audited: 2026-08-17.
